full_judgment:
Md Abu Tariq J: Defendant as appellant presented the above appeal against judgment and decree dated 28-8-05 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 104 of 2002, which decreed the suit as prayed for. 

 6. The learned trial Court initially framed issues and then tried the suit. The plaintiff examined three PWs and the defendant examined only one DW. The learned trial Court after examining the material evidences on record and other circumstances decreed the suit on contest vide the impugned judgment and decree. 

 7. Mr ASM Kamal Amrohi Chowdhury, learned Advocate for the appellant, submits that learned Joint District Judge erred in law in not applying his judicial mind properly to the provision of Specific Relief Act and wrongly decreed the suit. He further submits that plaintiff-respondent clearly violated the terms and conditions of the bainapatra as hopelessly failed to pay Taka 4,00,000 to the defendant No. 1 appellant within stipulated time of three months i.e. upto 15-5-99 and further amount of Taka 2,30,000 within next three months i.e. within 15-8-99, and as a result the bainapatra as well as baina money stands cancelled, as such, the trial. Court most illegally decreed the suit which is liable to be dismissed by this Division. 

 8. Mr Rabi Sankar Chakrabarty, learned Advocate, on the other hand, appearing on behalf of the respondent, submits that trial Court rightly decreed the suit on considering the papers and documents produced by the plaintiff and in the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 10. He lastly, submits that trial Court on considering all the papers and documents produced and in the facts and circumstances of the case, has believed the case of the plaintiff and accordingly, rightly decreed the suit which may be upheld by this Division. 

 13. Trial Court on considering all papers and witnesses adduced by both parties decreed the suit giving a direction upon the defendant No. 1 to register the land of schedule No. 1 in favour of the plaintiff within thirty days of receipt of the order on receiving outstanding Taka 5,30,000, otherwise the plaintiff shall be entitled to execute the deed through the Court in accordance with law. 

 14. Facts stated hereinabove need not be reiterated. Only question that is facing us is, whether the trial Court is well justified in decreeing the suit on considering the papers and documents and in the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 21. In view of the above elaborate discussion, we do not have any hesitation to say that the learned Joint District Judge has properly considered all the papers and documents and decreed the suit. 

 22. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without however any order as to cost with little modification of the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-8-2005 giving solatium money of Taka 5,00,000 more on consideration of present market value of the land.
